title: In a spectral space the generalizations of a quasi-compact set form an intersection of quasi-compact opens
statement: Let $X$ be a spectral space [def-weil-spectral-space] and let $E\subseteq X$ be a subset which is quasi-compact in the induced topology. Let $W=\{x\in X:\ \overline{\{x\}}\cap E\neq\emptyset\}$ be the set of points of $X$ that specialize to some point of $E$. Then $W$ is quasi-compact, and $W$ is the intersection of all quasi-compact open subsets $U\subseteq X$ with $E\subseteq U$; in particular $W$ is an intersection of quasi-compact open subsets of $X$.

source.place: Topology, Lemma 0A31 (label lemma-make-spectral-space, line 5005), implication (3) => (4) and the quasi-compactness of W shown in its proof (third paragraph); used in Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 0CAM (lemma-connected-topological, line 15071)

proof.text: $E\subseteq W$, and every open subset $U\subseteq X$ with $E\subseteq U$ contains $W$. For $e\in E$ we have $e\in\overline{\{e\}}\cap E$, so $e\in W$. Let $U$ be open with $E\subseteq U$ and let $w\in W$; choose $e\in\overline{\{w\}}\cap E$. Then $e\in U$ and $U$ is an open neighbourhood of the point $e$ of the closure of $\{w\}$, so $U\cap\{w\}\neq\emptyset$, i.e. $w\in U$. (Source: 'every point of $W$ specializes to a point of $E$ we see that an open of $W$ which contains $E$ is equal to $W$'.)

source.place: Topology, Lemma 0A31 (lemma-make-spectral-space, line 5005), proof, third paragraph: implication (3) => (4)

proof.text: $W$ is quasi-compact. Let $(V_j)_{j\in J}$ be open subsets of $X$ with $W\subseteq\bigcup_j V_j$. Since $E\subseteq W$ (step 1) and $E$ is quasi-compact, there is a finite $J_0\subseteq J$ with $E\subseteq V:=\bigcup_{j\in J_0}V_j$. $V$ is open and contains $E$, so $W\subseteq V$ by step 1. Hence finitely many $V_j$ cover $W$. (Source: 'Hence since $E$ is quasi-compact, so is $W$'.)

source.place: Topology, Lemma 0A31 (lemma-make-spectral-space, line 5005), proof, third paragraph: implication (3) => (4)

proof.text: If $x\in X\setminus W$ then $Z=\overline{\{x\}}$ is disjoint from $W$. Suppose $w\in Z\cap W$ and choose $e\in\overline{\{w\}}\cap E$. Since $w\in\overline{\{x\}}$, the closed set $\overline{\{x\}}$ contains $\overline{\{w\}}$, so $e\in\overline{\{x\}}\cap E$ and $x\in W$, a contradiction.

source.place: Topology, Lemma 0A31 (lemma-make-spectral-space, line 5005), proof, third paragraph: implication (3) => (4)

proof.text: For $x\in X\setminus W$ there is a quasi-compact open $U\subseteq X$ with $E\subseteq U$ and $x\notin U$. With $Z=\overline{\{x\}}$, the set $X\setminus Z$ is open and contains $W$ (step 3). Since the quasi-compact open subsets of the spectral space $X$ form a basis of the topology [def-weil-spectral-space], each $w\in W$ has a quasi-compact open $U_w$ with $w\in U_w\subseteq X\setminus Z$. As $W$ is quasi-compact (step 2), finitely many $U_{w_1},\dots,U_{w_n}$ cover $W$; their union $U$ is open, quasi-compact (a finite union of quasi-compact sets), contains $W\supseteq E$ (step 1), and $U\subseteq X\setminus Z$, so $x\notin U$ because $x\in Z$. (Source: 'Since $W$ is quasi-compact we can find a quasi-compact open $U$ with $W\subset U$ and $U\cap Z=\emptyset$'.)

source.place: Topology, Lemma 0A31 (lemma-make-spectral-space, line 5005), proof, third paragraph: implication (3) => (4)

proof.text: Conclusion. Let $W'$ be the intersection of all quasi-compact open $U\subseteq X$ with $E\subseteq U$ (this family is nonempty: $X$ itself is quasi-compact and open [def-weil-spectral-space]). By step 1 every such $U$ contains $W$, so $W\subseteq W'$; by step 4 no $x\notin W$ lies in $W'$, so $W'\subseteq W$. Hence $W=W'$ is an intersection of quasi-compact open subsets of $X$, and $W$ is quasi-compact by step 2. (Source: 'We conclude that (4) holds'.)

split_report.summary: Statement checked against Stacks 0A31 (3) => (4) and kept. Proof written in five steps following the third paragraph of the proof of 0A31: E ⊆ W and every open containing E contains W (opens are stable under generalization); W quasi-compact; closure of a point outside W misses W (transitivity of specialization); separation of such a point from W by a quasi-compact open, using that quasi-compact opens form a basis (definition of spectral space); conclusion. Every step is elementary from def-weil-spectral-space; no new node was needed, and the constructible topology (0A31 (1) => (2)) is not used for this direction. The earlier leanfinder record called IsCompact.of_subset_of_specializes an ingredient; it is the converse direction and does not apply (recorded). Two Mathlib searches added; no match.
